verseContext: Moses says this to a terrified people caught between Pharaoh's army behind them and the sea in front of them, before God opens a path.
title: A Way Through the Sea
subtitle: The sea in front, the army behind, and nowhere to go — which is exactly when God works
mainTruth: When God's people could do absolutely nothing, God did everything. Salvation is His victory, not ours.

read.title: Read Together
read.text:
God's people were free. They walked out of Egypt with everything they owned, and God Himself went in front of them — a tall pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night, so they always knew where He was.

Then the road ran out. In front of them was the sea, huge and deep and impossible. And behind them came a sound they had hoped never to hear again: Pharaoh had changed his mind, and his whole army was thundering after them.

The people were terrified. Sea in front. Army behind. Nowhere to run. They could not swim it, they could not fight, they could not go back. There was absolutely nothing they could do.

And Moses said: 'Do not be afraid. Stand still, and watch what God will do. The Lord will fight for you — you only need to be still.'

Then God moved. The pillar of cloud shifted round behind them and stood between His people and the army all night long. And God told Moses to lift up his stick over the water — and God sent a strong wind, and the sea opened. A wide dry path appeared straight through, with walls of water standing on either side.

All night God's people walked through the sea on dry ground. Every one of them came out the other side. And when the army tried to follow, the waters came back and the danger was gone for ever.

So God's people stood on the far shore, safe, and they sang. Not one of them had rescued themselves. That is what salvation is. God does it, and we stand still and trust Him, and then we sing.
read.childText: God's people were free! God went in front of them — a tall cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night. Then the road ran out. In front was the deep sea. Behind came Pharaoh's whole army! The people were terrified. They could not swim it and they could not fight. There was nothing they could do. So Moses said, 'Do not be afraid. Stand still — the Lord will fight for you!' Then God sent a strong wind, and the sea opened up. A wide dry path went straight through, with walls of water on both sides! All night God's people walked through and came out safe. Then they sang, because God had done it all.

discuss.title: Talk About It
discuss.question: What could the people do to save themselves?
discuss.parentGuide: The answer is nothing at all, and that is the doctrine — salvation is God's victory when His people are helpless. Watch out for the hero-swap here: Moses did not part the sea, God did, and Moses' stick was simply obedience. 'Stand still' is not laziness; it is trust when there is genuinely nothing left to try. Retrieve the Passover: rescued by the lamb, now rescued through the sea. Keep the army's end brief — the danger was ended, and God's people were safe. Paul later calls this a picture of baptism: going down into the water and coming out free.
discuss.familyQuestion: When has something felt impossible, and then worked out?

pray.title: Let's Pray
pray.guidedPrayer: God, You made a way where there was no way at all. Thank You that You fight for Your people. When we are frightened and there is nothing we can do, help us to stand still and trust You. Amen.
pray.childPrompt: Can you tell God about something that feels impossible?
prayerPoints: Tell God about something that feels impossible right now
Thank God that He fights for His people

remember.title: Remember This
remember.memoryVerse: God said: 'I will fight for you. You can be still.'
remember.tip: Hold both arms straight up like two walls of water, stand completely still for three seconds, then say: 'God fights for us!' Then walk through the gap between your arms.

doToday.title: Do It Today
doToday.action: Next time you feel worried today, stand still, take three slow breaths, and say: 'God fights for me.'
doToday.parentNote: This gives your child a physical action for the moment worry arrives, which is far more usable than a concept. Practise it once now while everyone is calm, so the body remembers it when they are not.
